readme_contract.audience: Developers who can read TypeScript and want a bounded environment for reviewing an agent-assisted change.
outcomes: Run and inspect the deterministic order service.
Make a bounded change and review its diff.
Use the local verification gate before accepting the change.
readme_contract.assessment: A learner explains the observed behavior and submits a verified, reviewable change.
readme_contract.safety_cost_boundary: The baseline is offline and credential-free; any Cursor or model use is optional and may incur provider cost.
readme_contract.completion_evidence: The learner can run make verify and describe the resulting passing service tests.

lab_contracts.objective: Inspect, run, and safely change a small deterministic order API.
setup: Run npm ci in this directory.
lab_contracts.expected_result: The tests pass and the local server exposes deterministic order routes.
lab_contracts.verification: npm test exits successfully before and after the learner's bounded change.
lab_contracts.rubric: The change is small, explained, and verified rather than accepted on agent output alone.
failure_modes: A change alters a route without updating its test.
extensions: Add a test for a new response edge case.
Review an agent-proposed diff before applying it.

readme_contract.thesis: A useful tool claim needs an observable failure path, not only a successful run.
prerequisites: Ability to read a small Python or TypeScript example
readme_contract.demonstration_exercise_route: Trace the article's proposed tool behavior, then design a licence-cleared public fixture before adding runnable code.
readme_contract.fixtures: No runnable fixture is included in Phase 1; a future fixture needs an approved public source and licence decision.
readme_contract.verification: Verify the map describes no local code and does not claim the article body is present.
readme_contract.next_learning_step: Choose a public, licence-cleared fixture and define the exact failure behavior before implementation.
